brief.title: Daymark task planner
brief.brief: Build Daymark, a small single-page daily task planner. It must be a complete standalone HTML document with inline CSS and vanilla JavaScript. No external URLs, assets, fonts, libraries, network requests, storage, or backend. State lasts until page reload. Use a distinctive, polished calm editorial design: warm off-white background, dark ink typography, restrained green accent, generous spacing, strong hierarchy, and thoughtful empty states. It must work at 390px and desktop widths with no horizontal overflow. Start with exactly three example tasks: Outline the launch plan (High), Take a walking break (Low), and Review the first draft (Medium). All start active. Provide a visible task title label and input id=task-title, a priority selector id=task-priority with values High, Medium, Low, and an Add task button id=add-task. Add task through the button or Enter. Trim whitespace and reject a blank title with a visible helpful error without adding a task. Preserve literal text characters in titles, including Focus; never interpret task titles as HTML. Each task row must have data-task-id and contain a real checkbox to mark completed and a button whose accessible name starts with Delete. Deletion and completion must target the correct task even after filtering. Completed tasks must look distinct. Provide filter buttons with ids filter-all, filter-active, filter-done and accessible pressed states. All shows all tasks, Active only incomplete tasks, Done only completed tasks. Search input id=task-search filters task titles case-insensitively and combines with the active filter. Show counters with ids count-total, count-active, count-done, each containing only a number. They count the entire task list, independent of filters/search, and update immediately after add, complete, or delete. Show a helpful empty state when no task matches. Use semantic HTML, visible labels, keyboard-operable controls, visible focus styling, readable contrast, and a polite live status region. Buttons must have meaningful accessible names. Task list container must have id=task-list. Include a small note that changes reset on reload. No misleading buttons or claimed cloud features.

design: One shared initial generation. Direct retains it. EGM and grounded each review that same draft with two fresh contexts, then receive one HTML revision call. No final output is hand-edited. HTML wrappers are constructed by the comparison app.
limits: Direct one attempt, no transport retry; each review allows one correction; each branch one HTML revision. No retry of truncated or invalid HTML. Runtime validation establishes citations and structure, not correctness.
limitations: One task, one trial; unequal compute by design. EGM is adapted to review an HTML implementation stored in the design field. This is not the full upstream EGM plugin or the previous design-review benchmark. Same requested model group, actual provider routes may differ.
presentation: Method names hidden initially, user can reveal them. Source is downloadable. No overall winner or accuracy percentage inferred from appearance.
